chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

There is nothing in the Scale heavier than the Salat (blessings) upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad. And indeed, when a man's deeds are placed in the Scale, it tilts due to them (his sins). So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) brings out the Salat upon him and places it in his Scale, so it outweighs them.

key_terms.الصَّلَاة: Blessings or prayers (specifically divine or prophetic blessings in this context)
key_terms.الْمِيزَان: The Scale of deeds on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.يَرْجَح: To outweigh or tip the balance

ai.seo_question: How do blessings upon the Prophet weigh against sins on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the metaphysical weight of Salawat, portraying it not merely as a ritual but as a decisive spiritual currency that can outweigh other deeds on the Day of Judgment. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as the Ahl al-Bayt serving as the intercessors whose connection to the believer tips the scales, reflecting the concept of their spiritual authority (Wilayah) in balancing human imperfection.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There would not be anything in the Scale (on the Day of Judgment) heavier than the Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammad, and that the man, his deeds would be placed in the Scale and it would tilt by it (due to the load of the sins). So the Salawāt would come out upon him and it would be placed in his Scale, so it would be outbalanced it (his sins)’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (a.s.) who has said the following: “

On the balance there will be no other thing as heavy as asking from Allah al-Salat (favors) for the Holy Prophet and his family. A man will place his deeds on the balance and it will tilt. Then he will bring forth his deed of asking from Allah al-Salat for the Holy Prophet and his family to place on the balance and it will weigh heavy in his favor.”
